Sam (Sales): Heads up — AcmeCorp POC failing behind corp proxy. Getting intermittent 502s and socket errors. Can we swarm?

Olga (Client Eng): Error details from their logs: `Error: socket hang up` and `ECONNRESET` when calling https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat. They run both Python and Node clients.

Iris - SolutionsEng: probably proxy related. Ask for client snippets and env (HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY) and whether proxy does NTLM or TLS interception.

Olga (Client Eng): Python example: `requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)` Node example uses fetch default. They set HTTPS_PROXY to corp proxy.

Devon (Platform SE): two quick items: 1) corp proxies often terminate TLS and inject their CA, which causes `unknown ca` unless the client trusts that CA. 2) streaming endpoints keep connections open — proxies may close idle connections after ~15s.

Iris - SolutionsEng: short repro steps: try a non-streaming simple generate first. For Node use https-proxy-agent and set keepAlive. For Python use `requests` with `Session()` and longer timeout. If proxy is NTLM, run a local shim like cntlm or ntlmaps to avoid TLS rewrap.

Olga (Client Eng): they confirmed NTLM and can't add corp CA to all hosts. CNTLM approach acceptable?

Devon (Platform SE): yes. CNTLM does NTLM auth and forwards via CONNECT. Example: run cntlm locally, point HTTPS_PROXY to http://localhost:3128, keep client TLS intact. That avoids TLS interception.

Iris - SolutionsEng: also recommend idempotency keys to avoid double-charges on retries and to let server dedupe. Add `Idempotency-Key` header with UUID.

Olga (Client Eng): after suggesting cntlm + increased timeout to 60s + retries with exponential backoff they ran tests. Most calls succeeded; a few long responses still got 502s.

Devon (Platform SE): those 502s on long responses are commonly the proxy dropping the connection mid-stream. Two mitigations: enable client keep-alive and chunked polling (if streaming problematic). For immediate POC: increase client timeouts to 120s and use non-streamed responses where possible.

Sam (Sales): buyer asked whether adding corp CA or using CNTLM breaks anything server-side or violates policies?

Iris - SolutionsEng: no server-side issues; we don't do cert pinning. Adding corp CA is customer-side only. CNTLM is fine for POC. If they require hardened setup, we can discuss Private deployment or dedicated network egress rules.

ci-bot: scheduled smoke test run at 1781234720 — all tests passed against api.redwood.ai.

Olga (Client Eng): confirmed CNTLM + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for dev machines fixed 95% of cases. Will add notes to POC runbook: detect proxy interception, recommend CNTLM, set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or requests verify path, increase timeouts, enable idempotency header and exponential backoff.

Sam (Sales): great — I'll update the deal doc and pricing slide with note about potential engineering time for proxy work.

Iris - SolutionsEng: I'll drop a gist with Python/TS examples and a short checklist in the POC folder. :thumbsup:

Olga (Client Eng): thanks team, moving to next validation.
